stem: Input solution EC remains stable, but root-zone EC rises during a period of much deeper dryback. What is the strongest interpretation?
choices: Assume the fertilizer formulation has changed and replace the nutrient concentrate, because root-zone EC should otherwise remain equal to input EC through the irrigation cycle
Conclude that water uptake has stopped and increase irrigation frequency immediately, because rising root-zone EC is sufficient evidence that roots are no longer taking up water
Lower root-zone water content can concentrate dissolved ions, so nutrition and irrigation data should be interpreted together
Interpret the higher EC as a specific micronutrient deficiency and increase trace elements, because concentration changes identify which nutrient is limiting
rationale: Root-zone concentration depends on both dissolved ions and water content. Deeper dryback can increase measured EC even when the incoming solution has not changed.
